newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked bonds end higher in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked bonds end higher in quiet trade.

text.p: Israeli unlinked bonds rose on Tuesday in very quiet trading, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.09 pct to 103.87
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.04 pct at 103.12
Volume was a low 101 million shekels with activity in the Makam falling to only 30 million shekels.

"CPI-linked bonds closed lower today led by a decline in short bonds," said Gila Shkury of Israel Discount Bank. "Analysts are predicting that inflation will decline dramatically during the next few months because of a sharp fall in housing prices."
Lower inflation forecasts caused a rise in unlinked bonds, she added.

"Inflation-linked bonds made a very big move but they cannot continue rising without fresh news. Overall, activity was mixed today and the market is expected to remain stable," said a trader at Tachlit Securities.

Dollar-linked bonds closed slightly higher after the dollar rose mildly against the shekel. In the local market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3670 shekels against 3.3660 shekels on Monday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
